title: The Larder of Stolen Plums
story: Deep in a sleeping giant's larder, Pottlegrim has stacked the village's stolen plum jam on tall shelves — 15 shelves with 24 jars on each. The gnasher won't fight; he bargains, and he insists on keeping 25% of all the jars as 'shelf rent'. He also admits, with a sticky grin, that 36 of the jars left over are already licked empty.
question: How many full jars of plum jam does Mr 6 carry back to the village?
solution: First the whole larder: 15 shelves × 24 jars = 360 jars.
Pottlegrim keeps 25%, so the village gets 75%: 360 × 0.75 = 270 jars.
Take away the 36 empty ones: 270 − 36 = 234 full jars.
praise: Counting the whole array of shelves first is exactly the right opening move — the 36 empty jars just needed to come off at the end.
hint: Start with the array: how many jars sit on all 15 shelves together? Then deal with the rent, then the empties.
victory: Mr 6 named 234 before Pottlegrim could finish his sticky sums, and the gnasher was so impressed he carried the crates to the door himself — and asked for a jam recipe instead of rent.
imagePrompt: A towering giant's pantry lit by one swinging lantern, shelves of purple jam jars climbing into shadow, a round sticky-pawed gnasher counting on his claws while a small numeral-6 knight points confidently at the shelves.
